svg.title: Datopsis lakehouse: Phase B identity architecture (target design)
svg.desc: Rauthy chosen 2026-11-13, Keycloak fallback. Human PKCE and machine client-credentials flows, Sail external token file, Lakekeeper JWT validation and PostgreSQL storage over verified TLS. Authorization and credential vending are not built.

LEGEND
Verified TLS: server certificate and hostname checked against the test CA
Dashed future boxes: not built; no authorization or vending claim
Arrows show requests; token and JWKS responses return over the same TLS connection.
③ File delivery is local, not a network hop. ④ Represents all API clients.
Phase A diagram details the proxy's approved 127.0.0.1 plaintext exception.
TOKEN FLOW · numbered alternatives converge at the catalog
① Human signs in with authorization code + PKCE; the OIDC client receives an access token.
② Trino and PyIceberg obtain machine access tokens with their own client credentials.
③ An external client obtains Sail's token; Sail reads its local token file, with no native grant.
④ Each API client sends its access token as a bearer token to Lakekeeper over HTTPS.
⑤ Lakekeeper fetches Rauthy's JWKS over HTTPS and validates the JWT; groups await Phase C.
Target only: main Integration still has login off; bake-off evidence does not qualify this full design.
